newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares fall, clearing system hampers trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares fall, clearing system hampers trade.

text.p: A new clearing system recently installed by the Cairo bourse continued to mystify the market on Monday and helped bring share prices off their highest level since April 1995, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index fell 0.88 points to 234.31 from Sunday's 17-month high of 235.19 points in low turnover of 21.01 million pounds ($6.18 million).

"It was very quiet. The system is very confusing and since it's much easier to put in buy orders than sell orders, prices get inflated artifically so we just didn't trade," said broker Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB stockbrokers.

Brokers said the popular milling sector managed broad-based gains on real demand with recent privatisation Central and West Flour Mills, the day's most active share, leading the way and rising 0.75 pounds to 47.75.
North Cairo Flour Mills gained 2.89 pounds to 112.01 in active trading while South Cairo Flour Mills rose 0.32 to 55.00. Only recent listing Upper Egypt Flour Mills shed 0.25 to 45.15 pounds.

But the clearing system hampered transactions in Memphis Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries, which enjoyed a brief rally early in the session only to end unchanged at 61.45 after brokers were unable to coordinate trade.
Drugs firm Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries was also among the day's busiest shares, rising 1.00 to 158.00.
Telemisr/Arab Radio Transistor and Electronic Supplies fell 0.65 to 32.03 after audited results showed their 1995/96 net after-tax profits fell to 10.340 million from 10.588 million a year earlier.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 364.86 points from 368.44 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 161.41 points from 161.42.
